div.p: Spatial econometrics relies on the spatial weights matrix to specify the cross-sectional dependence; however, the candidate spatial weights matrices might not be unique. This paper proposes a model selection procedure to choose a weights matrix from several candidates by using a Mallows type criterion. We prove that when the true weights matrix is not in the candidates, the procedure is asymptotically optimal in the sense of minimizing the squared loss; otherwise, the procedure can select the true weights matrix consistently. We then propose a model averaging procedure to reduce the squared loss. We also provide procedures for the spatial model with heteroscedasticity and endogenous regressors and the model with both spatial lag and spatial error. Monte Carlo experiments show that proposed procedures have satisfactory …nite sample performances. We apply the model selection and model averaging procedures to study the market integration in China using historical rice prices.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: Spatial econometrics study autocorrelation among cross-sectional units and have broad applications. 1 Among them, the spatial autoregressive (SAR) model proposed by Cli¤ and Ord (1973) has received the most attention. To estimate the SAR model, various estimation methods have been developed. 2 These estimation methods treat the spatial weights matrix as given and implicitly assume that the speci…cation of the spatial weights matrix is true, which means that the matrix in use is identical to the one in the data-generation process. However, because a spatial weights matrix is constructed from geographical or economic information to characterize the spatial dependence, the candidates for the spatial weights matrix might not be unique. Currently, there is no concise theory on how to …nd the true spatial weights matrix. Additionally, the true one may not be among the candidates of the weights matrices. The purpose of the current paper is to propose a model selection procedure to choose the true spatial weights matrix when the true one is in the candidate set and to choose the best one in the sense of minimizing squared loss when the true one is not in the candidate set. We also propose a model averaging procedure to further reduce the squared loss.

To select the true spatial weights matrix, using GMM estimates, Kelejian (2008) suggests a non-nested J-test for testing a null SAR model against a set of alternative models with di¤erent spatial weights matrices. His J-test is based on whether or not predictions based on alternative models signi…cantly add to the explanatory power of the null model. Kelejian and Piras (2011) suggest a modi…cation of Kelejian's J-test that uses available information in a more e¢ cient way, and Kelejian and Piras (2014) extend it to a panel data setting. Both Kelejian (2008) and Kelejian and Piras (2011) face shortcomings. If we reject the null model (using one of the spatial weights matrices) with more than one alternative speci…cation, there is no formal procedure proposed to select alternatives. Model selection by minimizing a criterion is an alternative to usual testing. For the commonly used information criteria AIC (Akaike, 1973) and BIC (Schwarz, 1978), the penalty 1 Early development in estimation and testing can be found in Anselin (1988Anselin ( , 1992)), Kelejian and Robinson (1993), Cressie (1993), Anselin and Florax (1995), Anselin and Rey (1997), and Anselin and Bera (1998), among others.

Lee (2003) chooses some speci…c IVs and obtains the best two-stage least square (B2SLS) estimators. Lee (2004) studies the asymptotic properties of the maximum likelihood (ML) and quasi-maximum likelihood (QML) estimators of the SAR model. For the SAR model, the spatial correlation can provide nonlinear moment conditions in addition to linear moments of IVs in the general method of moment (GMM) setting. Lee (2007) establishes the asymptotic properties of GMM estimators, which can be more e¢ cient than 2SLS estimators. The best GMM can be as e¢ cient as ML estimators (MLEs) when the true disturbances are normal. Liu et al. However, the approximation step is based on the assumption that the true data-generation process is contained in the candidate model (see Chapter 4 of Konishi and Kitagawa (2007) for details). This assumption would not hold under the setting of selecting the weights matrix in SAR, where the true spatial weights matrix might not be included in the candidate set. In addition, the di¤erence between penalties for a spatial model and a model without spatial e¤ects is only 2 or ln n, which does not use the information of the weights matrix. Our simulation studies also show that AIC and BIC do not perform well when the spatial e¤ect is zero. Another commonly used criterion is Mallows C p (Mallows, 1974), which is developed using linear regression models. In the current paper, we will extend Mallows C p to SAR models. Speci…cally, following the idea of Mallows C p , we propose a selection criterion by estimating expected squared loss. Hence, our criterion can be regarded as a type of Mallows criterion but di¤erent from Mallows C p because the new criterion has a more complicated form and is related to a candidate spatial weights matrix.

Unlike studies featuring the identi…cation of weights matrix, our focus is also on the true conditional mean of dependent variables, given independent variables. We show that the proposed procedure can select the true spatial weights matrix in the large sample sense if it is in the candidates. As a further step, we also propose a procedure for model averaging to reduce estimation error. We demonstrate that the proposed selection and averaging procedures are asymptotically optimal in the sense of achieving the lowest possible squared loss in a class of model selection and model average estimators, respectively. We also provide procedures for the spatial model with heteroscedasticity and endogenous regressors and the model with both spatial lag and spatial error.
We believe that our procedures are useful for empirical researchers who might have several spatial weights matrices available and do not have an explicit guide for which one to use.

The current paper is di¤erent from several other model selection problems in spatial econometrics, such as specifying spatial lag and spatial error models, or selecting the SAR model or matrix exponential spatial speci…cation (MESS). Debarsy and Ertur (2010) investigate how to distinguish two di¤erent spatial speci…cations in a panel data model setting, i.e., a spatial lag model or a spatial error model. Under the setting of panel model with both spatial lag and spatial error (SARAR), they construct …ve di¤erent test procedures: one joint test, two conditional tests and two marginal tests, for a …xed e¤ects panel model based on Lee and Yu (2010). Han andLee (2013a, 2013b) consider a J-test to distinguish SAR and MESS models, where the former implies a geometrical decline pattern of spillover e¤ect or externalities, while the latter exhibits an exponential decline pattern of spatial externalities. The current paper will focus mainly on selecting and averaging di¤erent spatial weights matrices.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows. Section 2 introduces the model and maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) of SAR models. Section 3 proposes the model selection procedure, and its asymptotic properties are proved. Section 4 studies the model averaging procedure. Section 5 provides extensions considering heteroscedasticity, endogenous regressors, and additional spatial errors. Section 6 conducts Monte Carlo experiments to investigate the …nite sample properties of model selection and model averaging procedures. Section 7 investigates the spatial weights matrix selection in studying the market integration using a historical dataset of Chinese rice prices. Section 8 concludes. Some algebra is presented in the Appendices. 3

div.head: Monte Carlo
div.p: We conduct a Monte Carlo experiment to evaluate the performance of the model selection (MS) and model averaging (MA) procedures in the current paper. Their performances under nonnormally distributed disturbances and endogenous spatial weights matrices are also investigated.

We also study alternative approaches, such as the J-test in Kelejian and Piras (2011), a direct estimation of high-order SAR models, AIC/BIC/Mallows C p / b C ori;s methods, and a heteroscedasticity case using GMM estimation, where b C ori;s is the original version of the criterion b C s (i.e., without adding the penalty term pen s ), which is de…ned in (10). Due to space limitations, detailed Monte Carlo results are found in the supplemental …le.

div.head: Conclusion
div.p: This paper proposes a model selection procedure to choose an optimal weights matrix from several candidates by using a Mallows type criterion. We prove that, when the true weights matrix is not in the candidates, the procedure is asymptotically optimal; otherwise, the procedure can select the true weights matrix consistently. This procedure will be useful for empirical researchers who might have several spatial weights matrices available and do not have an explicit guide for which one to use. We also propose a model averaging procedure to reduce estimation error. Monte Carlo experiments show that proposed procedures have satisfactory …nite sample performances, and an empirical example is illustrated.

If one uses our procedure to select the weights matrix and then derives the properties of parameter estimators by taking the selected matrix as given, the pre-test estimation problem can be involved; see discussions in Danilov and Magnus (2004). Therefore, the uncertainty that is introduced by the model selection procedure should be taken into account, which is of interest for future research. Also, the current paper considers only the SAR structure in a linear model with cross sectional data, and extensions of weights matrix selection to consider nonlinear covariate in an SAR model (see Su andJin, 2010 andSun et al., 2014) or panel data setting would be of interest.
